seed: Placing a measurement decides whether it is going across or down from wherever the pointer happens to be, and it keeps changing its mind as you move. So to measure from a baseline down to the top of a line of text that sits off to one side, you could not reach that text: the caliper flipped to measuring across before you got there. Holding shift now holds the direction the measurement is going in, exactly as it holds the line a placed caliper is on, so the pointer can travel sideways to the point you actually want to catch and only how far it got ALONG the held direction is taken. This walk places the same measurement five ways: free, held, held from after the crossover, let go of after the crossover, and held while the magnets still catch.

steps.note: THE PROBLEM, with nothing held. Foot A went down on the baseline at (500, 200) and the pointer went down to row 600 first, where the caliper was measuring DOWN, then travelled out to x 940 to reach the text. By then 440 across beat 400 down, so it flipped: the caliper measures ACROSS row 200 to x 940 and the text at row 600 was never reachable

THE CLAIM. The same travel with shift pressed while the caliper was measuring DOWN. The pointer still walked 420 out to x 940, well past the point where a free placement flips, and the measurement stayed vertical: feet (500, 200) to (500, 600), 400 raw pixels down, which is the baseline measured against text that is not underneath it

THE SECOND CLAIM. The pointer had ALREADY crossed over into measuring across before the key went down, and the key takes what is on screen at that moment rather than what the placement started as. So this one is horizontal, and it stays horizontal while the pointer drops another 300 down to (700, 900): feet (500, 200) to (700, 200)

THE THIRD CLAIM. Held down the whole way out to x 940, then the key is let go with the pointer sitting there. The direction goes straight back to being chosen from where the pointer is, with nothing carried over: feet (500, 200) to (940, 200), which is exactly what the free placement in stage 1 landed
A reference caliper lying along row 600, placed free of the magnets, so there is a horizontal line at y 600 for the next placement to catch

THE FOURTH CLAIM. Held going down, magnets on, and the pointer stopped 6 short of the row it was aiming at, at (940, 606). The magnet along the held direction still catches, so the foot takes y 600 off the reference caliper's line while the pointer's x 940 is simply not taken: feet (500, 200) to (500, 600)
